label: BigCommerce
terms_note: Any BigCommerce store owner can create a store-level API account in the control panel (no review); public apps go through the Developer Portal + OAuth; rate limit per store plan — Standard/Plus 150 requests per 30 s, Pro 450 per 30 s, Enterprise custom / unlimited plan; quota shared by all apps on the store; 429 with reset headers.

discovery.auth: token (store-level API account: static X-Auth-Token created by the merchant; app-level accounts: OAuth grant-code flow per installing store)

rate_limits: per-plan request quotas (rate-limits page opened; numbers behind JS)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes**.Confidence: **high** — official developer documentation opened by the auditor.
auth: 1. Store-level: merchant opens Settings › Store-level API accounts, creates a token with the minimum scopes (Products modify, Orders modify, Inventory modify, Webhooks default) → static access token + store hash.
2. App-level (multi-store): register the app in the Developer Portal; each installing store grants an OAuth code that is exchanged for a store-specific access token.
3. Pass the token as `X-Auth-Token` on REST and GraphQL Admin calls.

endpoints.purpose: Catalog V3 products (name, sku, price, inventory_level, inventory_tracking, variants)
endpoints.notes: reference page 403 in this pass — shape from the API-accounts index

endpoints.purpose: Orders V2 read, status update, shipments (tracking)

endpoints.notes: store/order/*, store/product/* — available to every API account type

reference.limits: Per store plan, refreshed every 30 s: Standard & Plus 150, Pro 450, Enterprise custom (Unlimited Rate Plan = no limit), dev/partner sandboxes by resource; every call = 1 unit; 429 with remaining / reset headers; back off exponentially. - Store-level accounts are for the merchant's own store; public apps must use app-level OAuth accounts. - Set scopes to the minimum needed (docs). - No app review for private/store-level use.
mcp_sdk: SDK: BigCommerce Developer Portal apps (OAuth) — https://developer.bigcommerce.com

fields.name: access_token
fields.help: Store-level API account access token (Settings > Store-level API accounts; scopes Products modify, Orders modify) sent as the X-Auth-Token header.

config_fields.name: store_hash
config_fields.help: Permanent store hash from the API path (https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{store_hash}/...), shown with the API account.

me.note: GET /stores/{store_hash}/v2/store returns the store's global settings {id, domain, secure_url, name, admin_email, currency, plan_name, ...}.

create_listing.note: POST /v3/catalog/products (required: name, type, weight, price): type=physical and weight=0 as in the documented example request; price, sku, description and inventory_level from the arguments. Response {data: product, meta}; `url` is the product's custom_url.url path on the storefront and `status` its availability (available|disabled|preorder). inventory_level only counts once inventory_tracking is `product` — set_inventory enables it. Stores with the V2 product experience also require `categories` (not sent); `currency`/`image_urls` are ignored (store currency; images via /images).

update_listing.note: PUT /v3/catalog/products/{product_id} with the given fields only (name, price, description, inventory_level); inventory_level applies when inventory_tracking is `product`. Response {data: product, meta}.

end_listing.note: PUT /v3/catalog/products/{product_id} {is_visible: false} hides the product from customers browsing the store (documented flag; reversible with is_visible=true). DELETE /v3/catalog/products/{id} (204) is irreversible and not used.

set_inventory.note: PUT /v3/catalog/products/{product_id} {inventory_tracking: product, inventory_level} sets product-level stock at the default location. `listing_id` (product id) is required: there is no update-by-SKU path (a GET /v3/catalog/products?sku= lookup is a second call), and variant-level stock uses /v3/catalog/products/{id}/variants/{vid} (not mapped).

list_orders.note: GET /v2/orders?page&limit&status_id&min_date_created (RFC-2822 or ISO-8601). `status` must be the numeric BigCommerce status id (status_id) from GET /v2/order_statuses, e.g. 2 Shipped, 10 Completed, 11 Awaiting Fulfillment; `total` is total_inc_tax, a decimal string, and date_created is RFC-2822. The V2 API answers 204 No Content when no order matches (an empty list).

mark_shipped.note: PUT /v2/orders/{order_id} {status_id: 2} — status id 2 is `Shipped` in GET /v2/order_statuses. `carrier` and `tracking_number` are NOT recorded: the shipment endpoint POST /v2/orders/{id}/shipments needs order_address_id and items[{order_product_id, quantity}] taken from the order, which the body form cannot supply.

not_offered.listing_metrics: No per-product analytics endpoint in the Catalog or Orders APIs (product `view_count`/`total_sold` are read-only fields on the product record, not a metrics call; store analytics are in the control panel only).
